finding.claim: deleteAccount computes the permission check canDelete(u, a) but discards its boolean result, so any caller can delete any account by id.
finding.source: Caller identity u and path parameter id in DELETE /accounts/{id} (AccountService.java:19-20). Any caller that reaches this method controls both.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at AccountService.java:23, a destructive write on an account the caller does not own.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id): u and id are supplied by the caller.
a = accounts.get(id) loads the target account with no owner scope.
canDelete(u, a) is a bare statement; its boolean result is dropped, so nothing throws or returns.
accounts.remove(id) runs unconditionally and deletes the account.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) implements the correct rule (admin or owner) but is unused on this path. No assertCanDelete call in deleteAccount; closeAccount (line 29) uses assertCanDelete, which shows the intended pattern. No other guard in the method. Route-level authn/authz is not in the provided code; if the HTTP layer enforces ownership before calling deleteAccount, impact drops, but nothing in this file shows that.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool that is discarded by the bare call at line 22, so it does not block. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17, which throws) is not called in deleteAccount (lines 20-24); it is only used by closeAccount at line 29. No other guard exists in the file, and no route-level authz is present in the directory (Grep found no DELETE routes, annotations, or filters).
verdict.reason: All trace lines match: line 22 discards canDelete's boolean (AccountService.java:9-11, 22), and line 23 calls accounts.remove(id) unconditionally, so any caller that reaches deleteAccount (line 20) can delete any account. The one caveat is that the endpoint's authentication and authorization layer is not in the provided code, so the attacker's required privilege is unverified, though the method itself performs no check.
